items.t: Front control arm bushings and tie rod ends wear out
items.job: Replace front lower control arms and tie rod ends, then align
items.note: Price covers both sides. Doing only one arm or one tie rod costs less.

items.t: Stalling or limp mode from throttle body or crank sensor faults
items.note: If the crank sensor is the cause instead, the repair costs less.

items.t: Underhood fuse and relay box (TIPM) faults
items.note: Rebuilt modules cost less. Have connectors checked first, since they can mimic a bad module.

items.t: Front and rear crossmembers can rust through (warranty extension X69)
items.note: Warranty extension X69 covers many 2008-2012 salt-belt vehicles. Check your VIN. Rear crossmember is extra.

items.t: Engine can shut down after a coolant temperature warning
items.job: Diagnose engine shutdown; test cooling system and sensors
items.note: No recall has been issued; a federal investigation is open.

items.t: Roof and sunroof water leaks (TSB)
items.job: Diagnose roof leak with a water test (bulletin 23-005-13)
items.note: Diagnosis only: the fix depends on what the water test finds (new sunroof drain tubes and grommets on earlier builds, or resealing the roof seams on later ones). The bulletin lists no labor time. RepairPal: $122–$179 for the diagnosis.

items.t: CVT overheats and cuts power
items.job: Change CVT fluid and check the transmission cooler
items.note: Based on KBB (no parts-plus-labor source found): dealer parts $136–$161, about an hour of labor, $303–$358 total at a dealer or $297–$348 at an independent shop. A failed CVT costs far more.
